title: Forecasted Demand Hedging and Contract Flexing Procedure
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard process for hedging forecasted demand, flexing (adjusting) contractual capacity commitments, and reconciling invoices to revenue recognition triggers. It covers operating principles, decision gates, an actionable runbook for procurement and finance, example scenarios with numeric impacts, and the technical hooks with our Billing Service and RevRec Engine. The procedure balances operational flexibility with revenue accounting controls to avoid surprise recognition or cash shortfalls.

Goals

- Reduce mismatch between forecasted consumption and committed capacity cost by at least 60% over a 12-month window.
- Ensure contract flex changes are compliant with revenue recognition rules (ASC 606 / IFRS 15 analogs used by RevRec Engine).
- Standardize a cross-functional decision path (Finance, Procurement, Product, Sales) for adjustments to commitments and pricing holdbacks.
- Maintain clear audit trail for external audits and internal forecasting.

Scope

Applies to:
- All capacity and committed GPU reservations (Dedicated) and multi-month buy commitments across hosted/dedicated/private products.
- Procurement actions that change monthly committed spend by > $25,000 or change capacity by > 10% of the existing commitment.
- Forecast adjustments that materially change monthly revenue recognition by +/- 5% of forecasted recognized revenue.

Exclusions:
- Routine one-off purchase orders under $5,000.
- Non-capacity software licenses without revenue recognition implications.

Key definitions

- Forecast Hub: Central forecasting dataset and UI used by Finance and Product.
- Commitment Window: Time interval (typically monthly) covered by a reserved capacity contract.
- Hedging Action: Any change intended to reduce the financial exposure from forecast variance (e.g., structured discounts, staged ramping, convertible credits).
- Contract Flexing: Formal amendment to an existing capacity contract to scale up/down committed units or adjust price.
- Pricing Holdback: Portion of invoiced amount deferred or conditioned on future usage milestones to align with RevRec triggers.

Roles & ownership

- Finance (Forecasting Lead): owns Forecast Hub, computes hedging recommendation, approves accounting impact. Primary contact: Priya Nambiar.
- Procurement: negotiates contract amendments and issues purchase orders in ProcureFlow. Primary contact: Marcus Lee.
- Product: validates technical capacity requirements and rollout schedule. Primary contact: Dana O'Connor.
- Legal: reviews material contract terms and amendment language. Primary contact: Arjun Patel.
- Billing Engineering: implements holdbacks and invoice metadata in Billing Service / Commitments API. Primary contact: Linh Tran.
- RevRec (Accounting Systems): configures revenue recognition rules and updates RevRec Engine. Primary contact: Miguel Santos.

Operating principles

1) Use conservative forecast bands: base / expected / upside with 40/35/25% weighting for procurement planning.
2) Prioritize flexibility over lowest initial unit cost when forecast uncertainty > 15% (measured as rolling 90-day MAPE).
3) Ensure every contract amendment includes metadata fields: amendment_reason, effective_date, capacity_delta, price_delta, pricing_holdback_percent, and accounting_treatment (defer/recognize).
4) Surface any proposed contract flex that changes RevRec recognition by > 5% of monthly revenue to Finance leadership for pre-approval.

Decision thresholds and gates

- Forecast accuracy SLO: Forecast Hub 30-day MAPE <= 15%. If violated for two consecutive periods, trigger mandatory hedging review.
- Contract flex threshold: capacity_delta >= 10% OR monthly committed cost delta >= $25,000 -> requires Finance + Procurement + Legal approval.
- Holdback threshold: pricing_holdback_percent > 10% -> requires RevRec sign-off.

Operational procedure (step-by-step)

1) Weekly Forecast Review (Finance)
   - Run Forecast Hub report: rolling 30/90-day MAPE, demand distribution (p50/p75/p90), and open commitments.
   - If 30-day MAPE > 15% OR p90 demand > committed capacity by > 20% within next 60 days, create a Hedging Recommendation.

2) Hedging Recommendation (Finance -> Product, Procurement)
   - Document options: (A) convert spot to short-term ramped commit; (B) add staged capacity with 30-day opt-out; (C) negotiate convertible credit (credit applied to future overage).
   - Include estimated P&L impact and RevRec treatment using scenario modeling (base/expected/upside). Attach model export (.csv).

3) Cross-functional Review Meeting (Ad hoc, required within 3 business days)
   - Attendees: Finance forecasting lead, Procurement rep, Product manager, Legal reviewer, Sales if customer-facing.
   - Approve one option and set action owner and timeline. Record decision in Forecast Hub as "Hedging Action ID".

4) Procurement Execution
   - Procurement creates amendment draft in ProcureFlow with amendment metadata pre-filled.
   - Legal reviews and clears final language within 48 hours for standard amendments.
   - Procurement issues PO / amendment and updates Commitments API with new capacity and holdback fields.

5) Billing & RevRec Implementation
   - Billing Engineering adds pricing_holdback_percent and holdback_conditions to invoices via Billing Service metadata.
   - RevRec updates RevRec Engine configuration: mapping amendment ID to accounting treatment and sets recognition schedule.
   - Finance validates journal entries in FDW (Finance Data Warehouse) and confirms deferred revenue balances.

6) Reconciliation (monthly, Finance)
   - Match invoices to commitments using Commitments API: ensure invoice_amount - holdback = recognized revenue per RevRec schedule.
   - Run a reconciliation report and flag any mismatches > 2% of invoice_amount.

7) Post-Implementation Review (30 days after amendment)
   - Measure actual cost vs. modeled cost and forecast variance. Capture lessons learned in Forecast Hub and tag the Hedging Action ID.

Templates & required fields

Procurement amendment metadata (table:
| field | required | description |
| amendment_id | yes | Unique amendment identifier (amend-YYYYMMDD-XXXX) |
| amendment_reason | yes | e.g., "hedge demand variance" |
| effective_date | yes | YYYY-MM-DD |
| capacity_delta | yes | positive or negative integer (GPUs) |
| price_delta | yes | decimal USD per unit |
| pricing_holdback_percent | conditional | integer 0-100; percent of invoice to holdback |
| holdback_conditions | conditional | free text; milestone or usage-based conditions |
| accounting_treatment | yes | "defer" | "recognize" |

Example amendment JSON to write to Commitments API (example snippet)
{
  "amendment_id": "amend-20270112-001",
  "effective_date": "2027-02-01",
  "capacity_delta": "+64",
  "price_delta": "-1.25",
  "pricing_holdback_percent": "10",
  "holdback_conditions": "10% held until 30-day cumulative usage >= 80% of new capacity",
  "accounting_treatment": "defer"
}

(Procurement should copy the snippet into ProcureFlow's amendment payload editor; Billing Engineering will ingest the same amendment_id.)

Accounting impact and controls

- Any amendment with accounting_treatment == "defer" must map to a deferred revenue schedule in RevRec Engine. Deferred balances should be reviewed by accounting weekly until fully recognized.
- Journal entry controls: dual review required for any amendment that increases deferred revenue by > $50,000. Approvers: Finance Lead + Controller.
- Audit trail: all amendments must include a linked Hedging Action ID and the Forecast Hub model export. Keep records for 7 years.

Monitoring, metrics, and SLOs

- Forecast Hub accuracy SLO: 30-day MAPE <= 15% (owner: Finance).
- Commitment invoice reconciliation SLO: monthly reconciliation mismatch < 2% (owner: Finance Ops).
- Amendment processing SLA: Procurement + Legal signoff within 72 hours for standard templates (owner: Procurement).
- Billing metadata ingestion SLA: Billing Service must surface new amendment metadata within 24 hours of Commitments API update.

Alerts (examples)

- Alert: "Forecast Hub MAPE breach" -> trigger: MAPE > 15% for 2 consecutive windows -> action: auto-create Hedging Action, notify Finance/Procurement/Product via Operations Slack channel #finance-procure-alerts.
- Alert: "Reconciliation delta" -> trigger: month-end mismatch > 2% -> action: Finance Ops page on-call and hold further procurement until remediation.

Example scenarios (numeric)

Scenario A: Upside demand outpaces forecast
- Current committed monthly cost: $400,000 for 256 GPUs.
- Forecast p90 indicates need for +64 GPUs in 45 days (expected additional monthly cost $120,000).
- Procurement negotiates staged 30-day opt-out ramp for +32 GPUs immediately and +32 GPUs after 30 days, pricing_holdback_percent = 10%.
- Modeled result: cash outlay month 1 increases by $60k, holdback $6k deferred; RevRec Engine recognizes incremental revenue when usage milestone met.

Scenario B: Demand shortfall
- Committed monthly cost: $300,000; near-term usage shows -20% vs commit.
- Hedging action: negotiate convertible credit equal to 50% of unused capacity that can be consumed over next 90 days or applied to overage at 80% face value.
- Accounting: convertible credit treated as contra-revenue when applied; initial recognition follows guidance in RevRec Engine based on when credit is consumed.

Governance and escalation

- Any dispute between Procurement and product about technical necessity escalates to Head of Platform (final arbiter for capacity need).
- Any change with revenue recognition impact > $250k requires Controller and CFO approval prior to execution.

Rollout checklist (first 90 days)

- Week 0: Publish this procedure and run a training session with Procurement, Finance Ops, Billing Engineering, and Legal.
- Week 2: Integrate amendment metadata schema into ProcureFlow and Commitments API.
- Week 4: RevRec Engine staging config updated to accept amendment_id mapping.
- Week 6: End-to-end test with a simulated amendment and reconciliation.
- Week 12: First post-implementation review and KPI check-in; iterate templates as needed.

Appendix A: Quick CLI snippet for Commitments API (curl)

curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwoodinfra.local/commitments/amendments -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"amendment_id":"amend-20270112-001","effective_date":"2027-02-01","capacity_delta":64,"price_delta":-1.25,"pricing_holdback_percent":10,"accounting_treatment":"defer"}'

Appendix B: Audit checklist (for Finance Controller)

- Verify amendment has Hedging Action ID and Forecast Hub export attached.
- Confirm Journal entries created / staged in FDW match RevRec schedule.
- Ensure dual approvers present for high-value deferrals.
- Confirm ProcureFlow contains signed amendment PDF and legal signoff.
